testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Brake harder than in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra braking force to activate the ABS.
Brake the same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
Brake with less force than in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way whether your vehicle has ABS or not. ABS helps prevent wheel lockup, but your braking technique stays the same.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: Release the gas pedal and push in the clutch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, release the gas pedal and push in the clutch to slow down gradually.

questions.question: Is texting while driving safer or more dangerous than talking on a cell phone?
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on a phone. It distracts you mentally and takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of retarders?

options.text: They may not be allowed in all areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be allowed in all areas.
questions.explanation: Retarders slow a vehicle and reduce brake wear. However, they can be loud and are not permitted in all locations.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand while the other rests.
With both hands for a firm grip.
Release it if the vehicle hits a bump.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands for a firm grip.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: A 40-foot load must be secured with a minimum of how many tie-downs?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. For a 40-foot load, you need at least four tie-downs. Always use a minimum of two tie-downs for any load.

questions.question: What can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab?

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.

questions.explanation: A faulty exhaust system is dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may mean the driver is:
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of impaired driving. A window open in cold weather may mean the driver is impaired from alcohol, drugs, sleepiness, or illness.

questions.question: If your personal vehicle license is revoked or suspended, can you get a hardship license for a commercial vehicle?

options.text: Yes, you can get a hardship license.
No, you cannot get a hardship license.
Your CDL will not be affected.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you cannot get a hardship license.
questions.explanation: If your personal vehicle license is revoked, canceled, or suspended, you cannot get a hardship license to operate a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, what can reduce how much you need to brake?
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. This helps your vehicle maintain a safe speed without using the brakes too much.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: If you do not drain air tanks, what could happen?

options.text: Water in the tanks could freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water in the tanks could freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: When driving, how often should you use your mirrors?

options.text: Only when there may be a problem.

questions.explanation: You must know what is around your vehicle at all times. Check your mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: What must interstate carriers display on their commercial trucks?
questions.explanation: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations require carriers to display their legal name or trade name on each commercial truck in their fleet.

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, what condition should the air compressor belt be in before each drive?
questions.explanation: Before each drive, check the air compressor belt on vehicles with air brakes. The belt should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve helps you control the vehicle better.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a foggy area?

options.text: Stop on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Slow down before entering fog. Use low beam headlights. Do not pass other vehicles or stop on the side of the road. It is safest to avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning happen most often?

options.text: When tire pressure is too low.
When tire tread is too deep.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tire pressure is too low.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely to happen on wet roads with low tire pressure and worn tire tread. Hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: How can you make your vehicle more visible during the day?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights during the day for the best visibility. Using high beam headlights can be dangerous around other drivers.

questions.question: When driving at highway speeds, how far ahead should you watch the road?
questions.explanation: Watch the road 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle to see obstacles and hazards. At highway speeds, this is about a quarter mile.

questions.question: To park as safely as possible, you should park:

options.text: So you must back up to leave.
So you can pull forward to leave.
On the side of a road, not in a parking lot.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous. Park so you can pull forward to exit your space whenever possible.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.question: Traction is important for:
questions.explanation: You cannot brake or steer without good traction. Keep your tires in good condition before driving.

questions.question: Alcohol usually:

options.text: Hurts your ability to judge distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hurts your ability to judge distance.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms basic driving skills including muscle control, reaction time, distance judgment, and night vision. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If the driving test route has no railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Do not need to do anything about crossings.
May need to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Must take the test again on a route with a crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route has no railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the correct crossing procedures at a practice location.

questions.question: If a police officer asks you to take a blood alcohol test:

options.text: You can refuse with no penalty.
You can refuse but must pay a $50 fine.
You will lose your CDL if you refuse.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will lose your CDL if you refuse.
questions.explanation: Most states have Implied Consent Laws. By driving on public roads, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test if asked. Refusing will cause you to lose your driving privileges.

questions.question: Anti-lock brake warning lights are:
questions.explanation: Vehicles with anti-lock brakes have yellow lights that show when the system is not working properly.

questions.question: A modulating control valve can control the:
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: During a trip, gauges are:

options.text: The only way to learn of vehicle problems.
One way to learn of vehicle problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: One way to learn of vehicle problems.
questions.explanation: During a trip, check gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights for signs of trouble.

questions.question: When encountering a railroad crossing during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate allowed for a triple combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: You need to know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle type. A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: A vehicle that stops at a green light may mean the driver:

options.text: Does not know the traffic rules

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. One warning sign is stopping in wrong places, like at green lights.

questions.question: Why should you check your tires often in very hot weather?

options.text: Air pressure increases as temperature rises
The tread wears down faster in hot weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure increases as temperature rises
questions.explanation: Heat raises air pressure inside tires. Pay close attention to tire condition and pressure when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should:
questions.explanation: Exhaust system parts must be in good condition with no leaks. A damaged exhaust system can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper area.

questions.question: You should NOT use your mirrors to:

options.text: Determine how fast you are traveling

questions.correctAnswerText: Determine how fast you are traveling
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly, especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, and making tight maneuvers. Do not use mirrors to check your speed.

questions.question: The brake pedal is part of which braking system?
questions.explanation: The service brake system is activated when the driver presses the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road
The tires grip the road better
The vehicle is easier to control

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose contact with the road and slide on a layer of water instead.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Go fast to clear the way for other drivers
Try not to use your mirrors

questions.explanation: Backing a large truck is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Use a helper if you must back up.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When roads are wet, snowy, or icy
When you are carrying a heavy load

questions.correctAnswerText: When roads are wet, snowy, or icy
questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow your vehicle and reduces brake use. However, retarders can cause wheel skidding on slippery surfaces. Turn off retarders when roads are wet, snowy, or icy.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Not be used by the driver
Only be used when it is wet outside
Be used to fully empty the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to fully empty the tanks
questions.explanation: Air brake systems contain water and oil from the compressor. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Open the air tank drains every day to remove this water and oil.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will:
questions.explanation: ABS is added to your braking system. It prevents brakes from locking up during hard braking. You should brake the same way in a car with ABS as in a car without it. ABS does not always shorten stopping distance.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Can damage your engine and transmission.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage your engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Always speed up slowly and smoothly. Avoid jerking your vehicle. Rough acceleration can damage your engine and transmission.

questions.question: The main reason to inspect your vehicle before a trip is:

options.text: To keep yourself and others safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep yourself and others safe.
questions.explanation: The main reason to inspect your vehicle before a trip is safety. You and other road users depend on it. State and federal laws require safety inspections before every trip.

questions.question: Brakes may get out of adjustment:
questions.explanation: Brakes can get out of adjustment quickly, especially from overheating. Check your brake adjustment often.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Assume the driver does not see you.
Wait for the other driver to signal it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: When passing another driver, cyclist, or pedestrian, always assume they do not see you. This keeps you safer.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Helps you stay awake on long drives.
Can damage your engine and transmission.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage your engine and transmission.
questions.explanation: Always accelerate smoothly and slowly. Avoid jerking your vehicle. Rough acceleration can damage your engine and transmission.

questions.question: If involved in an accident, which action is not recommended?

options.text: Moving your vehicle to the side of the road

questions.explanation: After an accident, protect the area, call authorities, help the injured, collect information, and report the accident. Leaving the scene is illegal and you can lose your license.

questions.question: If a heavy load is slowing you down, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle in second gear.

questions.explanation: Right lanes are for slower traffic. If a heavy load slows you down, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Drivers may use ____ red reflective warning triangles when stopped on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Place three red reflective triangles as warning devices when your vehicle is stopped on the road.

questions.question: Brake fade happens because of:
questions.explanation: If brakes are used too much, they overheat and become less effective. This is called brake fade.
